rows.grounds: locative of saṃhāra, indicating the time or state of cosmic dissolution
past participle of bhū, referring to entities that have come into being
accusative object indicating the state of dissolution or reabsorption
present active verb expressing movement or transition

items.question: Into what state do all sense-objects and beings pass during cosmic dissolution?
premises: Cosmic dissolution is a state in which manifested entities undergo reabsorption.
Sense-objects and beings that have come into existence are subject to this dissolution.
Their transition at dissolution is complete and without remainder.
items.inference: During cosmic dissolution, all sense-objects and beings pass entirely into a state of merging.
uncertainties: The precise ontological status of laya within the Siddhānta tattva scheme is not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: During dissolution, all sense-objects and beings go entirely into merging.
